result.overview: SAP S/4HANA Financial Accounting (FI) centers on the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), which merges general ledger, controlling, asset, and material-ledger line items into one multi-dimensional single source of truth, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation. Around that core sit Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, automatic payment runs), Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, dunning, incoming payments), Asset Accounting (ledger-based parallel valuation and depreciation), Bank and Cash Management (electronic bank statement processing, cash position), tax determination via tax codes and procedures, real-time financial statements drawn directly from the journal, and orchestrated period-end/year-end close (including the cloud Advanced Financial Closing product). Distinctive S/4HANA traits practitioners flag as essential include parallel ledgers for multi-GAAP accounting, document splitting for dimension-complete balance sheets, up to 10 parallel currencies, and posting-period control. Findings come from live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAPinsider, ERP Research, IBM, SAP Community) conducted for this task, supplemented by embedded knowledge of standard FI transactions.

capabilities.capability: General Ledger on the Universal Journal (ACDOCA)
capabilities.description: Single journal-entry table unifying FI/CO/AA line items with full dimensionality (cost center, profit center, segment, project), document principle, and immutable postings corrected by reversal.

capabilities.capability: Chart of accounts and fiscal year / posting period control
capabilities.description: Hierarchical chart of accounts plus fiscal year variants and posting period open/close control (OB52-style) that blocks postings into closed periods.

capabilities.capability: Multi-currency accounting and foreign currency valuation
capabilities.description: S/4HANA carries up to 10 parallel currencies per ledger (transaction, local, group, freely defined) with exchange-rate tables and period-end FX valuation posting realized/unrealized gains and losses.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only transaction + functional currency with rates table and realized/unrealized FX accounts; no group/additional parallel currencies or consolidation-style currency translation.
capabilities.later_path: Add extra currency amount columns per journal line plus a translation run, keeping the same rates-table and FX-account machinery.

capabilities.capability: Accounts Payable (vendor invoices, payment runs, aging)
capabilities.description: Vendor master data, invoice posting, open-item management, automatic payment program (F110-style proposal then run), and payables aging analysis.
capabilities.reason: Core AP (vendor bills, payment runs, aging) is planned; bank payment file formats (ISO 20022/NACHA) and withholding tax are not explicitly in v1.
capabilities.later_path: Layer payment-media file generation and withholding tax codes onto the existing payment-run engine.

capabilities.capability: Accounts Receivable (customer invoices, receipts, dunning, aging)
capabilities.description: Customer master data, invoice posting, incoming payment application and clearing, multi-level dunning procedures, and receivables aging.

Asset master records with depreciation areas tied to ledgers, acquisitions, multiple depreciation methods, intra/intercompany transfers, retirements with gain/loss, and assets under construction (CWIP).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 is 'asset accounting lite': register plus straight-line and declining-balance depreciation runs posting journals; no parallel depreciation areas, transfers, retirements with gain/loss, revaluation, or assets under construction.
capabilities.later_path: Extend the asset register with lifecycle events (transfer/retire/AuC settle) and per-ledger depreciation areas reusing the existing depreciation-run poster.

capabilities.description: House bank management, electronic bank statement import (MT940/CAMT.053) with automatic matching and clearing, bank communication (SWIFT/ISO 20022), cash position and liquidity forecast.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 covers bank reconciliation via CSV statement import with match suggestions only; no standard bank formats (MT940/CAMT), no auto-clearing rules engine, no cash positioning or liquidity forecasting.
capabilities.later_path: Add MT940/CAMT.053 parsers feeding the same import pipeline, then a cash-position report over bank-clearing accounts.

capabilities.capability: Tax handling (tax codes, determination, compliance reporting)
capabilities.description: Configurable tax codes within country tax procedures, jurisdiction-based determination (US sales tax, VAT), withholding tax, external tax engine integration, and statutory tax returns/reporting.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans line-level configurable tax codes (rate, jurisdiction, inclusive/exclusive) — the calculation core — but no withholding tax, no statutory tax return reports, and no external tax engine integration.
capabilities.later_path: Build tax-return reports as queries over tax-coded journal lines and add a pluggable external tax-calculation interface.

capabilities.description: Trial balance, balance sheet, P&L, and cash flow generated in real time directly from the Universal Journal via financial statement versions and embedded analytics, with no stored aggregates.

Orchestrated close: accruals, FX valuation, GR/IR regrouping, depreciation runs, balance carryforward into the new fiscal year, and task orchestration via closing cockpit / Advanced Financial Closing.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 has the enforcement primitives (period open/close at service and DB level, FX revaluation accounts, depreciation runs) but no year-end balance carryforward, accrual engine, GR/IR regrouping, or close task orchestration.
capabilities.later_path: Add a balance-carryforward job and a simple checklist-style close task list on top of existing period states.

capabilities.description: Multiple standard and extension ledgers valuing the same transactions under different accounting principles (IFRS/local GAAP), with document splitting producing dimension-complete balance sheets per profit center/segment.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans a single universal-journal ledger; no parallel/extension ledgers or document splitting — the boundary is single-GAAP, entity-level balance sheets only (dimensions exist on lines but are not balanced).
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a ledger dimension on journal entries so postings can fan out to parallel ledgers, then add a splitting rule engine at posting time.

capabilities.capability: Credit, collections and dispute management (Receivables Management/FSCM)
capabilities.description: Credit limit checks and scoring, collections worklists, and dispute case processing layered on top of core AR in S/4HANA.
capabilities.reason: Not in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 AR stops at invoices, receipts, dunning levels, and aging — credit/collections/disputes are S/4HANA add-on processes beyond core FI-AR.
capabilities.later_path: Add credit limits on the customer master with a posting-time check, then collections worklists driven by the existing aging data.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community/SAP PRESS blogs, and practitioner guides) for current S/4HANA 2025/2026. S/4HANA PP covers manufacturing master data (material master, multi-level BOMs, work centers, routings, production versions), demand management with planning strategies and planned independent requirements, MRP including the in-memory MRP Live engine, production order execution with shop floor control and confirmations, and capacity evaluation/leveling. It additionally ships lean/order-less execution models (kanban, repetitive manufacturing), process-industry variants (PP-PI), and embedded PP/DS for finite detailed scheduling and optimization. Atlas v1's plan covers the discrete-manufacturing core well (BOMs, work centers, routings, production orders with WIP accounting, a deterministic MRP run, rough capacity check) while deliberately omitting forecast-based demand management, operation-level confirmations, capacity leveling, kanban, repetitive manufacturing, PP-PI, and PP/DS-class finite scheduling — the same areas v1-grade systems typically defer.

capabilities.description: Defines product structure per level with components, quantities, scrap, validity dates/change numbers, and alternatives; basis for MRP explosion and order reservations.
capabilities.later_path: Alternative BOMs, engineering change management, and variant configuration can be layered on the versioned BOM model later.

capabilities.description: Master data for machines/lines/labor pools holding capacity (available hours), scheduling formulas, and costing links used by routings and capacity planning.
capabilities.later_path: Shift calendars, capacity categories, and cost-center activity rates can be added incrementally.

capabilities.description: Step-by-step operations assigned to work centers with standard values (setup, machine/run, labor) driving scheduling and product costing; combined with BOMs via production versions.
capabilities.later_path: Sub-operations, parallel/alternative sequences, and external-processing (subcontract) operations can be added to the routing model later.

capabilities.description: Create/release orders from planned orders, reserve components, goods issue to WIP, goods receipt to stock, status management, and WIP/settlement postings to accounting.
capabilities.later_path: Rework orders, co-products, availability checks at release, and order splitting can be added on the same order object.

capabilities.description: Recording yield, scrap, and actual setup/machine/labor times per routing operation, triggering backflush, WIP valuation, and progress tracking.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only order-level completion (issue to WIP, finish to stock, WIP journals); per-operation confirmations with actual time capture and scrap recording are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add a confirmation entity keyed to routing operations that posts actual times/quantities into the existing WIP journals.

capabilities.description: Net-requirements calculation exploding demand through BOM levels against stock and supply, generating planned orders/purchase requisitions; MRP Live runs it in-memory across plants in minutes with exception messages and rescheduling proposals.
capabilities.reason: The core deterministic run (sales-order demand + reorder points exploded against supply, producing planned orders) is planned; exception/rescheduling messages, MRP areas, multi-plant scope, net-change planning, and MRP-Live-class in-memory performance are not.
capabilities.later_path: Layer exception messages, pegging, and net-change/multi-plant runs onto the same planning engine without schema changes.

capabilities.description: Compares work-center load from planned/production orders against available capacity, then levels by dispatching/shifting operations to resolve overloads.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans capacity evaluation only (rough load vs available hours per work center); interactive leveling, dispatching, and finite scheduling are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add a dispatching board that re-dates order operations against a finite work-center calendar using the existing load data.

capabilities.capability: Demand management and planning strategies (PIRs, MTS/MTO)
capabilities.description: Maintains planned independent requirements from forecasts, applies planning strategies (make-to-stock, make-to-order, assembly), and consumes forecast against incoming sales orders.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 MRP consumes only direct sales-order demand and reorder points; forecast-based PIRs, planning strategies, and forecast-consumption logic are not planned, so make-to-stock forecast planning is impossible in v1.
capabilities.later_path: Add a PIR table with strategy/consumption rules as an additional demand source feeding the existing MRP run.

capabilities.description: Control cycles with container statuses (full/empty) that trigger replenishment via in-house production, external procurement, or stock transfer without MRP planning per bin.
capabilities.reason: No pull/lean replenishment is planned; Atlas v1 is purely push-based (MRP plus reorder points), which is the typical v1-grade boundary.
capabilities.later_path: Add kanban control cycles whose status changes generate the existing supply elements (production orders/purchase orders/transfers).

capabilities.description: Order-less, rate-based production on lines using run schedules and backflush confirmations against production versions, with period-based cost collectors instead of discrete orders.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 supports only discrete production orders; period/rate-based order-less execution and product cost collectors are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add run-schedule headers on production versions with backflush postings reusing BOM/routing and inventory movement logic.

capabilities.description: Advanced finite-capacity scheduling embedded in S/4HANA: sequencing, setup-matrix optimization, pegging, heuristics, and a graphical planning board for bottleneck resources.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 stops at rough infinite-capacity load checks; finite scheduling, optimizers, and planning boards are deliberately omitted, as in virtually all v1-grade ERPs.
capabilities.later_path: Bolt on a finite-scheduler service consuming routings, work-center calendars, and order operations via the existing APIs.

capabilities.capability: Process manufacturing (PP-PI: master recipes, process orders)
capabilities.description: Industry variant for batch/process industries using master recipes, resources, process orders, process instructions/PI sheets, and batch management integration.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 targets discrete manufacturing only; recipe/process-order semantics, PI sheets, and phase-based execution are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Model recipes and process orders as specializations of routings/production orders in a later industry add-on.

result.overview: In current S/4HANA (2025), MM-IM covers the material/product master, all goods movements (GR, GI, transfer postings, stock transfers) recorded in the unified MATDOC table, stock types and special stocks, physical inventory with cycle counting, and material valuation through the now-mandatory Material Ledger (standard price, moving average, FIFO/balance-sheet valuation), plus batch and serial number management and reorder-point replenishment. Warehousing is handled by embedded or decentralized EWM, whose basic tier covers storage-type/bin structures, putaway and stock-removal strategies, and handling units, while waves, slotting, labor management and MFS sit in the advanced (separately licensed) tier. Findings come from live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community, SAP PRESS and ERP consulting sources), cross-checked against embedded knowledge. Atlas v1 covers the transactional inventory core well (moves as single source of truth, MAV+FIFO costing, counts, lot/serial, reorder points) but deliberately stops short of stock-status/special-stock dimensions, standard costing, and the EWM execution layer (strategies, waves, handling units).

capabilities.capability: Material / product master with item types and multi-UoM
capabilities.description: Central material record (basic, purchasing, sales, MRP, accounting views) with material types and unit-of-measure conversions driving all logistics and valuation.
capabilities.later_path: Richer attribute views (classification, plant-specific MRP data) can be layered onto the item entity later.

capabilities.capability: Goods movements with movement types (GR, GI, transfer posting, stock transfer)
capabilities.description: Every stock change is a goods movement document (unified MATDOC in S/4HANA) that updates quantity and value in real time and drives FI postings.

capabilities.capability: Stock types and special stocks (unrestricted / QI / blocked; consignment, subcontracting, in-transit)
capabilities.description: Stock carries a usability status and ownership category so the same quantity can be quality-inspection, blocked, vendor consignment, at-subcontractor, or in transit.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 tracks quantity per warehouse/bin via stock moves but plans no stock-status dimension (QI/blocked) and no special-stock ownership categories such as consignment or subcontractor stock.
capabilities.later_path: Add status and ownership dimensions to stock quants/move lines, with status-change moves reusing the existing move ledger.

capabilities.capability: Physical inventory and cycle counting with difference posting
capabilities.description: Periodic, continuous and cycle-count procedures: create count documents, enter counts, post differences as valued goods movements reconciled to FI.
capabilities.later_path: Sampling-based inventory and ABC-driven count scheduling can be added on top of the count engine later.

capabilities.capability: Material valuation: moving average, standard price, FIFO (Material Ledger)
capabilities.description: Mandatory Material Ledger values every movement; price control S (standard, with price-difference variances) or V (moving average), plus FIFO/balance-sheet valuation and actual costing.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans moving average AND FIFO per item category with event-driven COGS posting, but omits standard costing with variance (price-difference) postings, which manufacturers treat as essential.
capabilities.later_path: Add a standard-cost method to the per-item-category costing engine, posting purchase/production variances to dedicated variance accounts.

capabilities.description: Lot-level tracking with batch master, expiry/shelf-life data and traceability, plus serial numbers tracking individual units across receipt, stock and issue.
capabilities.later_path: Automatic batch determination (FEFO, characteristics-based selection) and shelf-life blocking can be added as picking-time rules later.

capabilities.description: Reorder-point and safety-stock planning monitors stock levels and automatically generates procurement proposals (requisitions) when stock falls below threshold.
capabilities.later_path: Full MRP (time-phased, BOM-driven) belongs to a later manufacturing module; v1 reorder-point-to-draft-requisition covers the inventory-side core.

capabilities.capability: Warehouse structure: warehouses, storage types/sections, storage bins and quants
capabilities.description: EWM models a warehouse as storage types, sections, activity areas and bins with capacity attributes; stock is managed as quants at bin level.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans multi-warehouse and multi-bin stock keeping, but only a flat warehouse-to-bin model: no storage-type/section hierarchy, capacity checks, or activity areas.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce an optional storage-type/zone layer and capacity attributes on bins without changing the move ledger.

capabilities.description: Rule engines that determine the optimal bin for putaway (e.g. fixed bin, next empty bin, bulk) and for picking (e.g. FIFO, FEFO, partial-quantity-first).
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from Atlas v1: bins are chosen manually on stock moves; no strategy engine suggests or enforces source/destination bins.
capabilities.later_path: Add a rule-based bin-determination service invoked at stock-move creation, starting with fixed-bin and FIFO/FEFO rules.

capabilities.capability: Wave management and warehouse task/order processing
capabilities.description: Groups outbound picking work into waves and breaks execution into warehouse tasks/orders assigned to resources for high-volume fulfillment.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from v1; Atlas moves are executed directly with no intermediate task/wave layer. In SAP this is an advanced-EWM (extra license) feature, so it is not basic-tier core.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a warehouse-task layer between documents and stock moves, then add wave grouping and release rules on top.

capabilities.capability: Handling unit management (packing, nested HUs, SSCC labeling)
capabilities.description: Manages packed units (pallet/carton with packaging material + contents) as single objects through receiving, putaway, picking and shipping, including nesting and SSCC identification.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from Atlas v1; stock is tracked as loose quantities per bin with no pack/container object, even though HU management is part of SAP's basic EWM tier and core for shipping-heavy operations.
capabilities.later_path: Add an HU entity that wraps stock quants with pack/unpack/move-HU operations reusing the existing stock-move ledger.

result.overview: In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), QM covers quality planning (inspection plans, master inspection characteristics, sampling), quality inspection (inspection lots auto-created at goods receipt, in production, and at delivery), characteristic-level results recording, coded usage decisions that drive stock postings out of quality-inspection stock, and quality notifications/CAPA, plus certificates and supplier quality. PM-EAM (Asset Management) centers on technical objects (equipment installed on hierarchical functional locations), maintenance notifications feeding corrective maintenance orders with a phase-based lifecycle, preventive maintenance plans (time-, performance/counter-, and strategy-based) scheduled against task lists, and measurement points/counters for condition readings; the 2025 release adds enhanced Fiori order management, scheduling, and analytics. Findings are based on live web research (SAP Learning Journey, SAP Help Portal listing, ERP Research module guide, ASUG and NRX analyses of the 2025 release) supplemented by embedded S/4HANA knowledge where pages could not be fetched (SAP Help body content and one SAP Community post returned errors). Against the Atlas v1 plan, the GR-inspection-to-disposition flow, equipment register, and corrective/interval-based preventive orders cover a credible minimal core, but inspection plans, results recording, quality and maintenance notifications, functional locations, and measurement points are genuine gaps practitioners will notice.

capabilities.description: System-created inspection objects (from goods receipt, production, deliveries, or manual) that hold stock in quality inspection until decided
capabilities.reason: Only GR-origin lots via an inspection flag are planned; production/in-process, delivery, and manual lot origins plus sampling/sample-size logic are not
capabilities.later_path: Extend the existing lot object with additional origins (production order, delivery, manual) and sampling procedures

capabilities.capability: Inspection plans and master inspection characteristics
capabilities.description: Reusable task-list master data defining operations, characteristics, sampling procedures, and inspection methods per material
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 lots are plan-less binary accept/reject with no characteristic or sampling master data
capabilities.later_path: Introduce inspection plan + characteristic master data and assign plans to lots at creation

capabilities.description: Recording quantitative/qualitative results per inspection characteristic (single or summarized) with automatic valuation against tolerances
capabilities.reason: Depends on inspection plans/characteristics, which are cut; v1 captures only a lot-level accept/reject outcome, not measured values
capabilities.later_path: After plans/characteristics exist, add a characteristic-level results entry screen with auto-valuation

capabilities.description: Coded decision (UD catalog) closing the lot and posting quantities to unrestricted, blocked, scrap, sample, or return-to-vendor stock
capabilities.reason: Binary accept/reject with a stock move is planned, but coded UD catalogs, quality scores, and split-quantity postings (scrap/sample/return) are not
capabilities.later_path: Add UD code catalogs and multi-bucket quantity split posting on top of the existing accept/reject action

capabilities.description: Structured records of internal defects, supplier complaints, and customer complaints with tasks, causes, and corrective actions tracked to closure
capabilities.reason: No defect/complaint workflow in v1; a rejected lot only moves stock and does not open a tracked quality issue
capabilities.later_path: Add a generic notification/issue object (shared with maintenance notifications) linkable to lots, suppliers, and materials

capabilities.description: Certificates of analysis issued to customers or required from suppliers; quality info records gating procurement by vendor quality status
capabilities.reason: Not in the v1 plan; mainly needed in regulated industries and dependent on results recording, which is also cut
capabilities.later_path: Generate certificate documents from recorded results and add a vendor-material quality status check in procurement

capabilities.description: Equipment master records installed on hierarchical functional locations, carrying maintenance history, criticality, and structure
capabilities.reason: A flat equipment register is planned, but functional-location hierarchies, install/dismantle, and structure-based reporting are explicitly excluded
capabilities.later_path: Add a functional location entity with hierarchy codes and equipment installation/dismantle links

capabilities.description: Malfunction reports, activity reports, and maintenance requests that document problems and convert into maintenance orders
capabilities.reason: v1 creates corrective orders directly with no notification/request stage, losing breakdown reporting and MTBF/MTTR-style analysis
capabilities.later_path: Add a lightweight notification object convertible to an order, reusing the shared notification model

capabilities.description: Work orders against equipment with planning, execution, status lifecycle, completion, and cost capture (phase-based in current releases)
Time-based, performance/counter-based, and strategy plans whose scheduling automatically generates maintenance calls (orders/notifications)
capabilities.reason: Only fixed interval-based (time) preventive orders are planned; counter/performance-based and strategy plans are impossible without measurement points
capabilities.later_path: Once counters exist, extend the scheduler with performance-based cycles and packaged strategy plans

capabilities.description: Condition readings and usage counters on technical objects, documented as measurement documents and used to trigger maintenance
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; no condition readings or counter-driven triggers are planned
capabilities.later_path: Add a measuring point entity on equipment with reading documents that feed maintenance plan scheduling

capabilities.description: Reusable operation lists (general, equipment, functional-location task lists) assigned to maintenance items and orders to standardize work
capabilities.reason: Not in the v1 plan; v1 preventive/corrective orders would carry free-text work instead of reusable standardized operations
capabilities.later_path: Add a task list master assignable to maintenance plan items and copyable into orders

result.overview: Findings are from live web research (SAP Community, SAP Help Portal, SAP PRESS and SAP HCM consulting sources). In current S/4HANA, HR is delivered as "SAP HCM for SAP S/4HANA" (H4S4) — switched on by default from the S/4HANA 2025 release, with the old HCM compatibility pack retired — while SAP's strategic, go-forward HCM is the SuccessFactors cloud suite (Employee Central, EC Payroll, Time Tracking, Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, Performance, Compensation, Succession). H4S4 carries forward essentially the full SAP ERP HCM scope: Personnel Administration (employee master via infotypes), Organizational Management (org units/positions/jobs), Time Management (work schedules, time evaluation, CATS timesheet with cost-center/WBS allocation), localized gross-to-net Payroll with retro calculation and posting to FI/CO, plus ESS/MSS, benefits, compensation and some talent functions. Atlas v1's plan (employees with masked compensation, org structures and chart, leave accruals/approvals, time tracking with project/cost-center allocation, simplified non-compliant gross-to-net payroll posting a journal) covers the org, employee-master and leave cores well, covers timesheet capture and payroll-to-GL in reduced form, and deliberately leaves out talent, recruiting, benefits and jurisdiction-compliant payroll — the main honest gaps versus what HR practitioners consider a complete HCM suite.

capabilities.description: Central employee records via date-effective infotypes with personnel actions (hire/transfer/terminate) and protected sensitive data such as pay.
capabilities.later_path: Add date-effective history and formal hire/transfer/terminate actions on the existing employee entity.

capabilities.capability: Organizational management (org units, positions, org chart)
capabilities.description: Models org units, jobs, positions and reporting lines in one structure that drives workflows, approvals and authorizations.
capabilities.later_path: Extend later with date-effective org structures and job catalogs if needed.

capabilities.description: Absence types, quota accrual/entitlement, leave requests with manager approval workflow (ESS-driven in SAP).
capabilities.later_path: Later add collision checks with work schedules and quota carryover rules.

capabilities.capability: Time recording with account assignment (CATS-style timesheet)
capabilities.description: Cross-application timesheet recording working time against cost centers, projects/WBS and orders, feeding HR, CO and Project Systems.
capabilities.later_path: Planned core (capture + project/cost-center allocation) matches CATS; approval/transfer-to-costing flows can be hardened later.

capabilities.description: Work schedule rules, shift planning and rule-based time evaluation that derives overtime, premiums and balances feeding payroll.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans timesheet capture and leave only; no work-schedule rules, shift planning or rule-based evaluation of overtime/premiums.
capabilities.later_path: Add work-schedule calendars and a rules-based time evaluation step that feeds payroll inputs.

capabilities.description: Country-version gross-to-net payroll with tax/social-insurance compliance, retroactive accounting, payments and statutory reporting; fully available in H4S4 and as EC Payroll in SuccessFactors.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only a simple gross-to-net calculation explicitly flagged as not jurisdiction-compliant; no country legal rules, retro accounting, payment files or statutory reporting.
capabilities.later_path: Integrate certified third-party/localized payroll engines via connector, or ship country compliance packs incrementally.

capabilities.description: Posts payroll results to the general ledger with cost-center/labor-cost distribution so HR cost lands in accounting and controlling.
capabilities.later_path: Later refine with configurable wage-type-to-account mapping and accrual postings.

capabilities.description: Self-service for personal data changes, pay statements, time/leave entry and manager approvals/team views.
capabilities.reason: Leave approvals and time entry imply basic self-service, but no planned employee self-service for personal data, payslips, or manager team dashboards.
capabilities.later_path: Add ESS/MSS screens on top of existing HR APIs in the frontend once core records and payroll outputs exist.

capabilities.capability: Compensation management (pay structures and review cycles)
capabilities.description: Pay scales/grades, salary benchmarking and compensation planning/merit-review cycles (SAP PA-CM / SuccessFactors Compensation).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 stores only static masked compensation fields on the employee; no pay-grade structures or compensation review cycles.
capabilities.later_path: Add pay-grade/salary-band tables and a periodic comp review workflow over the masked fields.

capabilities.capability: Talent management (recruiting, onboarding, learning, performance, succession)
capabilities.description: SAP's strategic talent suite lives in SuccessFactors (Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, Performance & Goals, Succession); H4S4 retains legacy e-recruiting/learning.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 targets core HR/time/payroll-lite, and even SAP treats talent as a separate cloud suite rather than ERP core.
capabilities.later_path: Add as a separate talent module or integrate an open-source ATS/LMS against the employee and org APIs.

capabilities.description: Benefit plans, eligibility rules and enrollment with deductions flowing into payroll (SAP PA-BN / SuccessFactors Benefits).
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from v1; meaningful benefits administration depends on compliant payroll deductions, which v1 also lacks.
capabilities.later_path: Add plan/eligibility/enrollment objects feeding deduction lines once payroll gains real deduction handling.

capabilities.description: Headcount, turnover, absence and payroll-cost reporting via S/4HANA embedded analytics and SuccessFactors People Analytics.
capabilities.reason: v1 plan includes the org chart and operational record views but no HR KPI analytics (headcount trends, absence rates, labor cost).
capabilities.later_path: Build headcount/absence/labor-cost reports on the shared reporting module over HR and journal data.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Community 2025-release posts, SAP PRESS functional overviews, SAP Learning/Help pages), not embedded knowledge alone. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), Sales covers the full order-to-cash cycle: business-partner-based customer master, condition-technique pricing, pre-sales documents and contracts, sales order processing, (advanced) available-to-promise with backorder processing, outbound delivery and goods issue, billing with FI integration, FSCM-based credit management, and Advanced Returns Management, plus condition contract settlement (rebates), output management, intercompany/third-party flows, and Fiori-based fulfillment monitoring and analytics. The Atlas v1 plan covers the essential transactional spine (quote -> order -> delivery -> invoice with partial shipments, backorders, simple ATP, a credit-limit block, and RMA returns with credit notes) but deliberately simplifies the pricing engine, delivery execution, billing variants, and credit management, and omits contracts/scheduling agreements, output management, rebates, and intercompany/third-party processing.

capabilities.description: Central business partner with multiple roles and partner functions (sold-to, ship-to, payer, bill-to) feeding all sales documents.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans a customer master with core sales data, but not S/4HANA's multi-role business partner model with distinct partner functions (separate ship-to/payer/bill-to per document).
capabilities.later_path: Evolve the customer record into a party model with role assignments and per-order partner function overrides.

capabilities.description: Condition-technique engine: pricing procedures, condition types (price, discount, surcharge, freight, tax), access sequences, scales, and approval workflows.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans condition-style price lists by currency/customer group/date range plus discounts, but not the generalized access-sequence/pricing-procedure engine, quantity scales, freight/tax condition types, or price-approval workflows.
capabilities.later_path: Generalize price tables into condition tables with a pluggable access-sequence resolver and an ordered pricing procedure.

capabilities.description: Pre-sales quotation through sales order capture with document flow, copy control, statuses, and partial fulfillment tracking; the order is the single source of truth for logistics and billing.
Product availability check at order entry; aATP adds product allocation, alternative-based confirmation, supply protection, and mass backorder processing runs.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans a simple check against on-hand plus on-order with manual backorders, but none of aATP: no product allocation/quotas, alternative plant/substitution confirmation, supply protection, or prioritized mass BOP runs.
capabilities.later_path: Add a scheduled re-promising (backorder run) job and allocation buckets on top of the existing availability query.

capabilities.description: Outbound delivery documents with shipping point/route determination, picking, packing/handling units, goods issue posting, and EWM/TM integration.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans delivery documents with partial shipments and stock issue, but no picking/packing/handling units, shipping point or route determination, wave processing, or warehouse/transportation integration.
capabilities.later_path: Layer pick lists, packing/handling units, and shipping-point/route rules onto the delivery document later.

capabilities.description: Billing documents from deliveries or orders with FI revenue posting, plus collective billing, invoice splits, credit/debit memos, billing plans (milestone/periodic), and preliminary billing.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans per-delivery invoicing with FI posting and credit notes, but not collective billing runs, invoice split/merge rules, milestone or recurring billing plans, or preliminary billing.
capabilities.later_path: Add a collective billing-due-list job with split/merge rules, then billing plans as a follow-on.

capabilities.description: FSCM-based credit management (replaces classic SD credit): credit segments, rules-based scoring, real-time exposure across orders/deliveries/AR, and documented credit decisions with release workflow.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only a static credit-limit block at order confirmation; no exposure aggregation across open orders/deliveries/receivables, no rechecks at delivery, and no scoring or release workbench.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a finance-owned exposure ledger and a blocked-documents release queue, rechecking at delivery creation.

capabilities.description: Return orders with goods receipt back to stock and credit memos; ARM adds inspection codes, refund determination rules, and follow-up logistics such as return-to-vendor.
capabilities.later_path: Inspection dispositions, refund-determination rules, and vendor-return chains can be added on the RMA later.

capabilities.description: Long-term quantity/value contracts and scheduling agreements with release orders/delivery schedules drawn down against agreed limits.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 covers only the quote -> order flow; no long-term agreement document types or release-order consumption against contracted quantities/values exist in the plan.
capabilities.later_path: Add a contract document type with copy control to orders and quantity/value drawdown tracking.

capabilities.capability: Output management (order confirmations, delivery notes, invoices)
capabilities.description: Rule-driven generation and dispatch of sales documents as print/PDF/email/EDI, with form templates per document type; strengthened again in the 2025 release.
capabilities.reason: The Atlas v1 sales plan defines transactional documents but says nothing about rendering or transmitting them to customers, which practitioners treat as mandatory for go-live.
capabilities.later_path: Add template-based PDF/email rendering keyed by document type and customer as a cross-module output service.

capabilities.description: Rule-based condition contract settlement (successor to classic SD rebates) for retroactive customer rebates and commercial settlements.
capabilities.reason: No rebate accruals or settlement against sales volumes are in the Atlas v1 plan; only immediate order-level discounts are covered.
capabilities.later_path: Build on the condition engine later: accrue per qualifying invoice and settle periodically via credit memo.

capabilities.description: Automated cross-company sales with paired purchase/sales orders and intercompany invoices, plus third-party orders where the vendor ships directly to the customer.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 assumes a single selling entity shipping its own stock; no cross-company document pairing or vendor drop-ship triggering from sales orders is planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add order-triggered purchase requisitions (drop-ship) first, then paired intercompany order/invoice generation.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP Learning/certification syllabi, and consulting sources), completed June 2026. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), Sourcing and Procurement (MM-PUR) covers the full procure-to-pay cycle: business-partner-based supplier master data, purchasing info records, purchase requisitions (now with Fiori self-service apps), RFQs and quotation comparison, purchase orders, goods receipt, and logistics invoice verification with 3-way match, tolerances, and payment blocking. Approvals run through either classic classification-based release strategies or the newer flexible workflow, applicable to PRs, POs, contracts, scheduling agreements, and RFQs. Framework agreements (quantity/value contracts, scheduling agreements with delivery schedules), source determination (source lists, quota arrangements, info records), and supplier evaluation round out the area; certification weightings confirm master data, the PR-to-PO process, and GR/invoice verification as the practitioner-essential core. Atlas v1 plans the essential discrete P2P chain end-to-end but deliberately defers outline agreements, automated source assignment, and supplier evaluation.

capabilities.description: BP-based supplier records with purchasing and company-code views: payment terms, currency, partner functions, and blocking at central/FI/purchasing levels.
capabilities.later_path: Later add partner functions (ordering address vs. invoicing party) and granular block levels.

capabilities.description: Vendor-material master data holding time-dependent prices/conditions, planned delivery times, and tolerances used to default PO data; 20-25% of the certification master-data weighting.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 'approved items' on the vendor master captures the vendor-item link but not time-dependent pricing conditions or lead-time data that S/4HANA info records default into POs.
capabilities.later_path: Extend the vendor approved-items table with price, valid-from/to, and lead-time fields and use them to default PO lines.

capabilities.description: Internal demand documents (manual or MRP-generated) requesting a quantity of material/service by a date, converted to RFQs or POs; 2025 adds the 'My Purchase Requisitions - New' Fiori app and service-period items.
capabilities.later_path: MRP-generated requisitions arrive when the manufacturing/planning module lands.

capabilities.description: Request quotations from multiple suppliers, record quotations, compare prices, and convert the winning quote into a PO.
capabilities.later_path: Multi-bidder price-comparison views and rejection letters can be layered onto the v1 RFQ document.

capabilities.description: The central external purchasing document with item-level pricing, delivery dates, account assignment, change management, and output to suppliers; anchors PO history (GR/IR).
Receipt posting referencing the PO that updates stock and valuation, writes PO history, and feeds GR/IR clearing for the 3-way match.
capabilities.later_path: Atlas plans GR in the v1 chain; stock/valuation postings are owned by the inventory module.

capabilities.description: Match supplier invoice against PO and goods receipt, apply tolerance keys, block payment on variance, and post the AP liability with GR/IR clearing.
capabilities.later_path: Configurable tolerance groups, invoice-release workflow, and ERS (evaluated receipt settlement) are natural follow-ons; AP posting itself lives in finance.

capabilities.description: Classification-based release strategies (up to 8 release codes keyed on value, plant, material group, doc type) plus the newer flexible workflow, covering PRs, POs, contracts, scheduling agreements, and RFQs.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans data-driven value-threshold rules only; S/4HANA's essential release strategy also keys on multiple characteristics (plant, material group, document type), supports multi-step approver chains, and applies to more document types than the PR/PO chain.
capabilities.later_path: Generalize the threshold-rule schema into condition records (field/operator/value) with ordered multi-approver steps applied per document type.

capabilities.description: Longer-term agreements with target quantity or value against which release orders draw down, with header/item conditions and release documentation.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from the Atlas v1 list; v1 covers only the discrete requisition-to-PO chain with no outline-agreement document type or drawdown tracking.
capabilities.later_path: Add a contract document type referencing vendor and items with committed qty/value, and let POs reference it as release orders that consume the commitment.

capabilities.description: Outline agreements with delivery schedule lines (often MRP-maintained, with JIT/forecast releases) replacing many discrete POs in repetitive/direct procurement.
capabilities.reason: Explicitly excluded from Atlas v1; no document exists for schedule lines or releases, so repetitive direct-procurement scenarios are not supported in v1.
capabilities.later_path: Model as a contract variant carrying dated schedule lines that goods receipts consume directly, added alongside MRP integration.

capabilities.description: Automatic proposal/assignment of supply sources (info records, contracts, source lists, quotas) to requisitions, enabling automated requisition-to-PO conversion.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1's vendor-master 'approved items' provide manual approved-source data, but there is no automatic source proposal on requisitions, no quota arrangements, and no contract/info-record sources to determine against.
capabilities.later_path: Add a source-assignment service that matches open requisition lines to approved vendor items (later contracts) and supports one-click or automatic PO creation.

capabilities.description: Scoring suppliers on price, quality, and delivery performance plus embedded Fiori analytics (procurement overview, spend KPIs).
capabilities.reason: Not in the Atlas v1 plan; classed by SAP itself as an advanced feature (15-20% certification weighting) and not required to run the core P2P cycle.
capabilities.later_path: Compute supplier scorecards from existing GR (on-time/quantity) and invoice (price variance) history in the reporting module.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP PRESS, and ERP consulting sources, June 2026). In current S/4HANA, Controlling is no longer a separate ledger world: FI and CO are merged into the Universal Journal (table ACDOCA), so every posting carries cost center, profit center, project/WBS, order, and profitability-segment dimensions, and all CO reporting is a real-time projection of that single table; cost elements have become G/L accounts. The practitioner-essential core comprises cost center accounting, profit center accounting, internal orders (deprecated in S/4HANA Cloud in favor of project cost collectors), product cost planning and cost object controlling (standard cost estimates, WIP, variance calculation, settlement, increasingly event-based), Margin Analysis (account-based CO-PA in the journal, replacing costing-based CO-PA), universal allocations (distribution/assessment/overhead), activity types with internal activity allocation, and cost center planning/budgeting, with Material Ledger actual costing as an optional deepening. Atlas v1's design — dimensions on journal lines, cost/profit centers with allocation rules, manufacturing-fed WIP and finish-to-stock, and ledger-projected cost-center and margin reports — matches the architectural core of S/4HANA CO and its cloud-edition direction (including replacing internal orders with projects), but leaves activity-rate machinery, planning/budgeting, variance decomposition, and multi-dimensional margin segments for later.

capabilities.capability: Universal Journal merge of FI and CO
capabilities.description: Single line-item table (ACDOCA) where every posting carries all CO dimensions; cost elements are G/L accounts; FI/CO reconciliation eliminated by design.
Cost center master data, primary cost capture on postings, secondary cost flows via allocations, and cost center actuals reporting.
Profit center derived onto every journal line, enabling management P&L and segment reporting by profit center directly from the Universal Journal.

Cost collectors for internal measures (marketing campaigns, small capex, events) with planning, budgeting/availability control, and settlement to receivers; deprecated in S/4HANA Cloud in favor of project cost collectors.
capabilities.reason: Atlas deliberately mirrors S/4HANA Cloud's 'Principle of One' by covering the cost-collector role with projects/WBS instead of a separate order object, but order-specific machinery (order types, statistical orders, settlement rules to cost centers/assets, budget availability control) is not stated in the plan.
capabilities.later_path: Extend projects with settlement rules, budget/availability control, and settlement-to-asset postings rather than introducing a separate order object.

capabilities.description: Cost rollup over BOM and routing producing standard cost estimates with cost component split, costing runs, and standard price release for inventory valuation.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans manufacturing-fed product costing (actual costs, WIP, finish-to-stock valuation) but does not state a BOM/routing cost-rollup engine, cost component split, or standard price release/costing-run machinery.
capabilities.later_path: Add a cost-rollup service over BOM/routing data that produces standard costs with a component split, used to value finished-goods receipts and compute variances.

capabilities.description: Actual cost capture on production orders, WIP calculation, variance calculation by category, and settlement to stock/P&L/CO-PA; S/4HANA increasingly posts these event-based instead of at period-end.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans the core flow — WIP journals and finish-to-stock postings, which matches S/4HANA's modern event-based direction — but variance decomposition (input price/quantity, resource usage, lot size), scrap analysis, and settlement profiles are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add variance categorization computed from journal deltas at order close, posting categorized variance lines to the ledger and the margin report.

capabilities.description: Account-based profitability by market segment (product, customer, region, channel) stored on Universal Journal lines, with COGS component split and attributed margin; replaces costing-based CO-PA, which SAP no longer develops.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans a margin-by-product report projected from the ledger — the right account-based architecture — but only the product dimension; customer/region/channel segments, COGS split by cost component, top-down distribution, and realignments are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Widen journal lines with additional market-segment attributes (customer, region, channel) derived at posting time and add segment-level margin reports over the same ledger projection.

capabilities.description: Rule-based periodic distribution and assessment cycles moving costs between cost centers, profit centers, and profitability segments; S/4HANA unifies these in the Universal Allocation framework with Fiori apps.
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans allocation rules on cost centers and profit centers posting through the journal, which is the practitioner-essential core; allocation to margin-analysis segments and plan-data allocation are the main S/4 extras not mentioned.
capabilities.later_path: Add margin-segment-context and plan-data allocation cycles on the same rule engine.

capabilities.capability: Activity types and internal activity allocation
capabilities.description: Activity type masters with planned rates (machine/labor hours) driving direct activity allocation and secondary cost flows from cost centers into production orders.
capabilities.reason: No activity-type master, rate planning/calculation, or rate-based secondary cost postings appear in the Atlas plan; production cost capture is implied to be direct journal entries without rate machinery, so conversion-cost absorption from cost centers has no planned mechanism.
capabilities.later_path: Add activity types with planned rates that generate secondary-cost journal lines from production confirmations, crediting the supplying cost center and debiting the order.

capabilities.description: Plan data on cost centers and other CO objects (table ACDOCP, Fiori import, SAC integration) enabling plan/actual variance reporting and plan allocations.
capabilities.reason: The Atlas v1 plan covers only actuals; no plan ledger, budget entry, or plan/actual comparison is mentioned, yet plan-versus-actual on cost centers is a core controlling activity for practitioners.
capabilities.later_path: Add a plan-line ledger parallel to the journal and extend the cost-center and margin reports with plan/actual/variance columns.

capabilities.description: Material Ledger is mandatory in S/4HANA for multi-currency/parallel inventory valuation; optional actual costing periodically revalues inventory and COGS at actual costs.
capabilities.reason: Not mentioned in the Atlas plan; actual costing is an optional deepening in S/4HANA (mandatory only as the multi-currency valuation substructure), so omitting it from v1 is a defensible cut.
capabilities.later_path: Add a periodic actual-cost roll-up job that recomputes inventory and COGS values from accumulated journal lines and posts revaluation entries.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal PS documentation, SAP Community EPPM release blogs for S/4HANA Cloud 2502/2508, and SAP PRESS practitioner articles), supplemented by embedded S/4HANA knowledge for structuring. S/4HANA Project System manages internal, capital-investment, and customer projects through hierarchical work breakdown structures (WBS) and optional networks/activities, covering structure planning, scheduling, cost and revenue planning, budgeting with availability control, execution postings (time via CATS, procurement, goods movements), and period-end close via settlement and results analysis / event-based revenue recognition. In current S/4HANA (2025/2026) the area spans classic PS (on-premise/private cloud) and the Fiori-based Enterprise Projects and Professional Services Projects in Enterprise Portfolio and Project Management (public cloud), the latter pairing project control with event-based revenue recognition and milestone-linked billing. The Atlas v1 plan (WBS as costing objects, time and purchases postable to WBS, a project cost report) covers the execution-side core - structures and actual-cost collection - but deliberately omits the planning and financial-close layers: networks/scheduling, cost planning, budgeting/availability control, settlement, results analysis/revenue recognition, and customer-project billing are all out of scope for v1.

capabilities.description: Hierarchical project definition with WBS elements as account-assignment/costing objects, maintained via Project Builder or Fiori project apps with statuses and templates.
capabilities.later_path: Templates, status management, and mass-change tooling can be layered on the same WBS entity later.

capabilities.description: Task-level model beneath the WBS: activities with durations, work, relationships (dependencies), confirmations, and material components for logistics-driven projects.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 explicitly excludes networks; the v1 model is WBS-only cost collection with no activity/task layer.
capabilities.later_path: Add an activity entity under WBS elements with relationships and confirmations, then attach scheduling and material components.

capabilities.description: Forward/backward scheduling of dates across WBS and networks, project planning board (Gantt), critical path, and milestones that can trigger billing or workflows.
capabilities.reason: Scheduling is explicitly not in the v1 list and depends on the network/activity layer, which is also excluded.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce basic/forecast dates on WBS and activities plus a scheduling engine and Gantt view once networks exist.

capabilities.description: Planned costs per WBS element via hierarchy planning, cost-element planning, unit costing, or Easy Cost Planning, used as the baseline for budgets and variance analysis.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 collects only actual costs on WBS; no plan versions or planned-cost entry are in the plan, so the cost report has no plan/actual comparison.
capabilities.later_path: Add a plan-cost table keyed by WBS element and period, then extend the project cost report to plan-vs-actual.

capabilities.description: Original budget, releases, supplements/returns per WBS (CJ30 family) with active availability control that warns or blocks postings when assigned funds exceed tolerances.
capabilities.reason: Budgeting controls are explicitly excluded from the v1 list; v1 has no budget object and no posting-time funds check.
capabilities.later_path: Add a budget amount per WBS with tolerance rules evaluated in the posting pipeline before actuals commit.

capabilities.description: Employees record working time against WBS elements (or network activities) via timesheet; approved time posts labor cost to the project at an activity rate.
capabilities.later_path: Approval workflows and posting to network activities can follow once those features exist.

capabilities.capability: Procurement and expense postings to projects
capabilities.description: Purchase requisitions/orders, supplier invoices, goods movements, and journal entries account-assigned to WBS elements, including commitment tracking and project stock.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans actual purchase and expense postings to WBS, but PR/PO commitment tracking and project stock / project MRP are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Derive commitment records from open purchase orders assigned to WBS, then add project-stock segments in inventory.

capabilities.description: Period-end settlement of WBS costs to receivers - cost centers, assets under construction/fixed assets (investment projects), profitability segments (CO-PA) - via settlement rules.
capabilities.reason: Settlement is explicitly excluded from v1; collected costs remain on the WBS with no period-end transfer to receivers.
capabilities.later_path: Add settlement rules per WBS and a periodic settlement run reusing the finance allocation/posting engine.

capabilities.description: WIP calculation and POC-based revenue recognition for customer projects; classic results analysis in PS, or event-based revenue recognition with real-time Universal Journal postings in modern S/4HANA.
capabilities.reason: No revenue recognition or WIP/POC valuation of project costs is planned in v1; v1 projects are pure cost collectors.
capabilities.later_path: Implement event-based recognition postings in the finance module triggered by project cost and billing events.

capabilities.description: Linking sales order items to billing WBS elements with milestone billing and resource-related (time-and-material) billing generating billing documents from project activity.
capabilities.reason: Not in the v1 list; there is no planned sales-order-to-WBS link or billing generated from project time/expenses.
capabilities.later_path: Link sales order lines to WBS elements, then generate resource-related billing proposals from posted time and expenses.

capabilities.description: Hierarchical cost reports per project/WBS with plan, actual, and commitment columns, line-item drilldown, and real-time Fiori/HANA project financial overviews.
capabilities.reason: v1 plans a project cost report over actuals by WBS, but without plan or commitment columns and without the broader drilldown/overview suite, it is a reduced subset.
capabilities.later_path: Extend the report with commitment and plan columns and line-item drilldown as those data objects are added.

capabilities.description: Percentage-of-completion measurement per WBS/activity and earned value metrics (BCWS/BCWP/ACWP) comparing progress against plan and budget.
capabilities.reason: Depends on cost planning, budgets, and scheduling, none of which are in v1; also not considered core by most practitioners outside EPC/engineering industries.
capabilities.later_path: Compute POC and earned value from plan-cost and confirmation data once planning and scheduling layers exist.

result.overview: Cross-cutting platform concepts in S/4HANA (2025/2026) are the architectural primitives every functional module relies on: the Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as the single financial line-item table replacing separate FI/CO/AA/ML tables; document flow with predecessor/successor links viewable in the Document Relationship Browser; the mandatory unified Business Partner model (CVI-synchronized customer/vendor views); the BRF+/Adobe Forms output management framework; configurable number ranges per document type; the roles/profiles authorization concept (PFCG on-premise, business roles and catalogs with restrictions in Cloud); and the client (MANDT) field on nearly every table on-premise, replaced by tenant isolation in S/4HANA Cloud SaaS. Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP Learning, and consulting sources) supplemented by embedded S/4HANA knowledge for change documents, workflow, and extensibility. Atlas v1 deliberately inherits the two load-bearing patterns (Universal Journal, document flow) and covers tenancy, RBAC, audit, and numbering, while consciously deviating on the Business Partner model and deferring output management, workflow, and extensibility.

capabilities.capability: Universal Journal (ACDOCA) as single source of truth
capabilities.description: One line-item table unifying G/L, controlling, asset accounting, material ledger, and profitability analysis, eliminating FI/CO reconciliation; plan data mirrored in ACDOCP.
Every business document records its preceding and follow-on documents (quote -> order -> delivery -> invoice -> accounting doc), navigable as a chain in the UI.

Single mandatory master-data object for customers and vendors; CVI synchronizes BP roles to customer/vendor views, enabling one party to be both, with shared addresses, relationships, and time-dependent data.
capabilities.reason: Deliberate deviation: Atlas v1 keeps separate vendor and customer master tables; customer/vendor master data itself is planned, but there is no unified party object, no shared roles/relationships, and no single identity for an entity that is both customer and supplier.
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a thin party/business-partner table that links existing customer and vendor records as roles, without restructuring the two masters.

capabilities.capability: Output management (determination rules, channels, form templates)
capabilities.description: BRF+ rule-driven determination of output type, recipient, channel (print/email/EDI/XML), and form template (Adobe Forms with master templates), with output status, queue, and reprocessing across all document types.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only basic document rendering; the rule-based determination framework, multi-channel dispatch (email/EDI), template management, and output status/retry queue are explicitly not in the v1 list.
capabilities.later_path: Add a rule-driven output determination service (document attributes -> channel + template + recipient) with pluggable channel adapters and a retryable output queue.

capabilities.description: Configurable number intervals per document type with internal (system-assigned sequential) or external assignment; non-overlapping ranges and gapless sequences where legally required.
capabilities.later_path: Add external number assignment and per-fiscal-year ranges later if conversion/legal scenarios demand them.

capabilities.description: PFCG roles bundling authorization objects on-premise; business roles composed of business catalogs with read/write restrictions (org-level values like company code, plant) in S/4HANA Cloud.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans the RBAC core (JWT auth, roles -> permissions -> resources stored as data), but S/4HANA's field/org-value restrictions (scoping a permission to specific company codes, plants, etc.) and segregation-of-duties analysis are not in the v1 list.
capabilities.later_path: Extend permission records with attribute/scope filters (org-unit values) evaluated alongside the tenant filter, then layer SoD rule checks on role assignments.

capabilities.description: On-premise: client (MANDT) key on nearly all tables isolates independent business environments in one system; S/4HANA Cloud: dedicated tenants on shared infrastructure with strict isolation.
Change documents (CDHDR/CDPOS) record who changed which field from what to what on master and transactional objects, plus security audit log, supporting compliance and audits.
capabilities.later_path: Add read-access logging for sensitive fields as a later compliance increment.

capabilities.capability: Extensibility framework (custom fields, key-user and side-by-side extensions)
capabilities.description: In-app/key-user extensibility for custom fields and logic on released business contexts, plus side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP via released APIs and events, all upgrade-stable.
capabilities.reason: No custom-field or extension mechanism appears anywhere in the Atlas v1 plan; v1 ships fixed schemas only.
capabilities.later_path: Add JSONB custom-field columns with metadata-driven validation on core entities, plus webhook/event hooks per document type.

capabilities.description: Cross-application workflow (classic SAP Business Workflow and Fiori flexible workflows) for approvals and multi-step processes, e.g. PO release, journal entry verification, with My Inbox integration.
capabilities.reason: No approval/workflow capability is in the Atlas v1 plan; documents post directly without configurable release strategies, which practitioners consider a core control in procurement and finance.
capabilities.later_path: Add a generic approval service (document type + condition -> ordered approver steps) driving a status field that blocks posting until approved.

capabilities.description: Stable, versioned OData/SOAP APIs (SAP Business Accelerator Hub) and business events for integrating S/4HANA with external systems; the backbone of clean-core integration.
capabilities.reason: The Atlas v1 cross-cutting scope defines internal patterns (journal, flow, tenancy, auth) but lists no public API contract or event emission for external integration.
capabilities.later_path: Publish the existing internal REST endpoints as a versioned public API and emit domain events (document created/changed) to a message bus or webhooks.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community 2025-release blogs, SAP Fiori design system docs, and consulting sources such as PIKON). In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), this area covers the Fiori design system (Horizon theme, SAPUI5/Fiori elements controls), the role-based launchpad organized into spaces and pages with app/KPI/insight tiles, standard floorplans (list report, object page, overview page, analytical list page, worklist), and embedded analytics built on the CDS virtual data model: analytical queries, Smart Business KPI tiles with thresholds and drill-down, multidimensional reports, and self-service query creation - all running live on transactional data with insight-to-action navigation into transactions. The 2025 release adds Fiori 4.0 touches: AI-assisted enterprise search, Joule integration, smart summarization, and AI-personalized My Home insight cards. Atlas v1 covers the essential core of the role-based home page, role dashboards, and tabular self-service reporting; it plans reduced subsets of the component library, floorplan patterns, semantic layer, KPI framework, and drill-down analytics; and it omits enterprise search, per-user personalization/variants, and AI-assisted UX entirely.

capabilities.capability: Role-based launchpad home with spaces/pages and app/KPI tiles
capabilities.description: Single entry point where business roles determine visible spaces, pages, and tiles, including dynamic tiles showing live KPI numbers

capabilities.capability: Fiori design system and UI component library (Horizon, SAPUI5 controls)
capabilities.description: Consistent, responsive, accessible design language and a large control set (smart tables, forms, charts, cards) reused across all apps
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans a focused in-house kit (data grid, form builder, kanban, dashboard cards, document-flow viewer), not a full design system with theming tokens, accessibility standards, and the breadth of SAPUI5 controls
capabilities.later_path: Grow the kit into a documented design system: theme tokens, a11y audit, and new controls added as app screens demand them

capabilities.capability: List report + object page floorplans (transactional work pattern)
capabilities.description: Metadata/annotation-driven filterable list pages paired with detail/edit object pages, including draft handling and table variants
capabilities.reason: Atlas's data grid and form builder cover hand-built list+detail screens, but there is no metadata-driven floorplan generator, draft persistence, or saved table variants
capabilities.later_path: Add a schema-driven page generator that renders list+detail CRUD pages from entity metadata, then layer in drafts and variants

capabilities.description: Role-specific card-based pages (charts, lists, KPIs) giving a one-stop operational overview with navigation to detail apps

capabilities.capability: Analytical list page and multidimensional reporting
capabilities.description: Hybrid chart+table pages and pivot-style reports with interactive drill-down across dimensions (org, time, product, region)
capabilities.reason: Atlas's report builder yields a flat group-by grid with CSV export; no interactive pivoting, drill-down paths, or combined chart+table analysis UI is planned
capabilities.later_path: Add a pivot/drill-down UI and chart rendering on top of existing report-builder queries

capabilities.capability: CDS virtual data model and analytical queries (live semantic layer)
capabilities.description: Layered, reusable CDS views over live transactional data exposing governed analytical queries with measures, hierarchies, and calculated columns - no data replication
capabilities.reason: Atlas's report builder queries raw entities directly, which preserves the live-on-transactional-data principle, but there is no reusable layered view model, calculated/restricted measures, or hierarchies
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a versioned semantic layer (named reusable views and measures) that the report builder, dashboards, and KPI tiles all consume

capabilities.capability: Smart Business KPI framework (Manage KPIs and Reports)
capabilities.description: Key users define KPIs with thresholds/targets (red/amber/green), publish them as launchpad tiles, and drill down from the KPI to detail
capabilities.reason: Atlas ships a fixed set of KPI tiles and dashboard cards; end-user KPI authoring, threshold/target rules, color states, and publish-to-home are not planned
capabilities.later_path: Add a 'manage KPIs' admin screen where a KPI = saved report query + threshold rules, publishable as a home-page tile

capabilities.capability: Self-service query creation and export (Query Browser, custom analytical queries)
capabilities.description: Business users browse available queries and build tabular reports by choosing entity, columns, filters, and groupings, with export to spreadsheet
Generic semantic-object navigation lets users jump from any KPI, card, or report line straight into the underlying transaction; document flow visualizes linked documents
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans a document-flow viewer component, but no generic deep-link/intent framework wiring dashboard cards and report rows to the owning app screens
capabilities.later_path: Define per-entity URL route conventions (deep links) and wire dashboard cards, KPI tiles, and report rows to them

capabilities.description: Launchpad header search spanning apps and business objects (orders, customers, materials, invoices), AI-assisted as of S/4HANA 2025
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only per-report filters; no global cross-entity search or app finder exists anywhere in the plan
capabilities.later_path: Add a global search endpoint over key entities plus a header omnibox that deep-links into list/detail pages

capabilities.description: Per-user saved filter/layout variants, rearranging home tiles and My Home insight cards, and key-user adaptation of screens without code
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 home pages, dashboards, and grids are role-defined and static; no per-user variants, tile rearrangement, or screen adaptation is planned
capabilities.later_path: Persist per-user grid/filter variants and home-tile layout as JSON preference records keyed by user and screen

capabilities.capability: Joule and AI-assisted UX (NL navigation, smart summarization, easy filter)
capabilities.description: Embedded AI assistant for natural-language navigation, summaries, AI-built insight cards, and AI-assisted filtering across Fiori apps (Fiori 4.0)
capabilities.reason: Flagship 2025 differentiator but not yet baseline-essential, and largely premium/optional even in S/4HANA; nothing AI-related is in the Atlas v1 plan
capabilities.later_path: Once report-builder and search APIs exist, attach an LLM assistant that translates natural language into report definitions and deep links

capabilities.capability: Single-core delivery with industry activation (business function sets / switch framework)
capabilities.description: Most former IS add-ons are merged into one S/4HANA codebase ('industry to core'); industry behavior is activated per system via business function sets and switches (largely irreversible, one industry set per instance).
capabilities.reason: Atlas templates toggle modules and apply presets at tenant creation, but there is no deep switch layer that changes the behavior of shared module code per industry (e.g., retail switch altering core MM logistics flows).
capabilities.later_path: Add a feature-flag/behavior-variant layer inside modules keyed off the tenant's industry template.

capabilities.description: Activated industry switches re-label core objects across the UI (Material becomes Article, Plant becomes Site/Store, Customer becomes Patient in IS-H).

Industries get extended or first-class master data: retail article master with generic articles/variants and site (store/DC) master, healthcare patient master, EC&O equipment master, merchandise category hierarchies.
capabilities.reason: Typed custom fields (JSONB + metadata registry) extend core entities, but Atlas v1 plans no first-class industry entities such as article variant matrices, store hierarchies, or a patient demographics object.
capabilities.later_path: Ship industry entities as optional modules built on the metadata registry, starting with retail article/site.

capabilities.description: Vertical process suites on top of the core: retail merchandise management (assortments, allocation, promotions, seasonality), EC&O Equipment & Tools Management, professional-services Commercial Project Management and resource/time-expense flows, utilities billing (IS-U).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 templates only configure existing horizontal modules; no industry-specific process logic of any kind is planned.
capabilities.later_path: Post-v1 industry process packs as optional modules layered on core (e.g., a retail pack adding assortment/promotion flows).

capabilities.capability: Preconfigured industry best-practice content applied at provisioning
capabilities.description: SAP Best Practices / SAP Activate deliver per-industry preconfiguration: chart of accounts, tax settings, units of measure, number ranges, org-structure and approval defaults, activated as scope items at system setup.

capabilities.capability: Metadata-driven field extensibility surfaced across the UI
capabilities.description: Key-user extensibility adds typed custom fields to core objects and propagates them into apps, lists, and analytics without modification of the core (clean-core principle).

Industry solutions embed regulation: country-specific healthcare billing rules, public-sector funds/grants management, utilities regulated billing and metering, industry revenue-recognition methods (POC for construction/services).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 templates carry only default tax codes; no industry- or country-specific statutory logic, regulated billing, or POC revenue recognition is planned in the industry layer.
capabilities.later_path: Country/industry compliance packs per module once a localization framework exists, prioritized by shipped templates.

capabilities.description: S/4HANA covers roughly 25 industries across discrete/process manufacturing, retail/fashion, consumer products, utilities, oil & gas, banking, insurance, public sector, telco, A&D, healthcare, EC&O, professional services and more.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 ships 5 templates (manufacturing, retail, professional-services, healthcare, construction); deep verticals like utilities, banking, or oil & gas need far more than configuration templates.
capabilities.later_path: Grow template coverage via community-contributed YAML templates, pairing deep verticals with later process-pack modules.

capabilities.description: SAP's current strategy pairs a clean core with SAP Industry Cloud: partner solutions on BTP extend or replace vertical functionality side-by-side (e.g., partners taking over patient management as IS-H is discontinued by 2030).
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans no plugin/extension API or marketplace through which third parties could ship industry functionality; templates are first-party YAML only.
capabilities.later_path: Define a stable plugin API plus template packaging so third parties can publish installable industry packs.

capabilities.description: S/4HANA manages industry activation over the system lifecycle: transportable business-function activation, irreversibility rules, and conversion checks (always_on/always_off restrictions) during upgrades.
capabilities.reason: Idempotent template application at tenant creation is planned, but there is no template versioning or safe re-application/upgrade of templates to existing live tenants.
capabilities.later_path: Version templates and add a migration-aware re-apply command that diffs template state against live tenant config.

result.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community/learning content, and ERP consulting sources, June 2026). SAP's S/4HANA industry approach folded most former IS add-ons into a single codebase ('industry to core'), covering roughly 25 industries whose functionality is activated per system through business function sets and the switch framework — activation is largely irreversible, one industry function set per instance, and industry-specific LoB functions are licensed separately from the Enterprise Management core. What the industry layer actually varies is substantial: terminology (Article vs Material, Site vs Plant), industry master data models (retail article/site, patient, equipment), entire vertical process suites (merchandise management, EC&O Equipment & Tools Management, professional-services Commercial Project Management, IS-U billing), regulatory content, and preconfigured SAP Best Practices content applied at setup. The current 2025/2026 direction adds a clean-core posture where deep vertical needs increasingly move to SAP Industry Cloud partner extensions on BTP — notably SAP is discontinuing healthcare IS-H by 2030 in favor of partner solutions. Atlas v1's YAML template layer maps well to the configuration-content slice of this area (terminology overrides, CoA/tax/UoM/numbering/approval presets, module toggles, typed custom fields) but plans none of the vertical process logic, industry master data objects, regulatory content, or partner extension ecosystem that practitioners associate with SAP industry solutions.

result.notes: The research-date template variable arrived as literally "undefined", so the doc states June 2026 (taken from the research overviews). Most surprising: Project System is the thinnest area (8 of 12 capabilities out of scope — v1 projects are pure cost collectors) and QM/PM has only 1 fully covered capability; also a notable tension exists between the cross-cutting workflow engine being out of scope while procurement claims partial approval/release coverage via value-threshold rules.
